bank13_16bit_column_analysis.executed_operation: SEC; LDA low[Y]; SBC $03BB; STA $1E; LDA high[Y]; SBC $03BC

bank13_16bit_column_analysis.implication: The branch tests whether the high byte of the signed/modular 16-bit difference is zero. Only values whose difference from $03BB/$03BC lies in 0..255 continue to the B58B[Y] path.
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.fourth_column: B58B[Y] is then loaded and transferred to Y before JSR $1F84.
bank13_16bit_column_analysis.caution: This proves a range/window comparison against a 16-bit runtime base, but does not yet identify the physical meaning of either quantity.

runtime_base_03bb_03bc.important_result: $03BB/$03BC is not an arbitrary pointer loaded from ROM. It is a runtime-computed 16-bit quantity.

de84_decoder.exact_register_contract: A selects destination tile/address; X/Y are source pointer; RAM $32 is outer block count.
de84_decoder.header: At each outer block, source[0] is split: low nibble -> $34; high nibble + 1 -> $35.
de84_decoder.stream: Source pointer is advanced before reading payload bytes. Payload bytes are written to $2007. $35 counts down on payload writes; when it reaches zero, the current byte can be emitted repeatedly under $34. X starts at 16 and controls the block's output progression; source pointer and $32 advance/control subsequent blocks.
de84_decoder.destination: A is shifted left four times with carry accumulated into $33, then $33 and shifted A are written to $2006.
de84_decoder.correction: DE84 is not a raw 16-byte tile copier. It is a compact CHR stream decoder/uploader with nibble-coded run behavior.
de84_decoder.implication: Recovering tiles 4F-52 requires decoding the source stream, not copying 64 contiguous ROM bytes.
